questions.prompt: Which statements about arrays and pointers are true?
options: `sizeof(arr)` for an array is the size of the whole array in bytes
`sizeof(ptr)` for a pointer is the size of an address
An array name can be re-assigned to point elsewhere
A pointer variable can be re-assigned to point elsewhere
questions.explain: The array name is not a modifiable variable: it always denotes the same block. A pointer is a variable and can point anywhere. `sizeof` on a pointer does not know how many elements it points to.
option_notes: True (when `arr` is the actual array, not a parameter).
False: you cannot assign to an array name.

questions.explain: Indices start at 0: an array of 5 elements has the indices 0 to 4.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Partial initialisation.)
questions.explain: When an initialiser has fewer values than the array, the remaining elements are set to zero.
With 6 ints of 4 bytes `sizeof(v)` is 24, and dividing by the size of one element gives the number of elements, 6. (It only works on a real array, not on a pointer parameter.)
`m[row][column]`: row 1, column 0 holds 4 and row 0, column 2 holds 3.
The array name converts to a pointer to its first element: `*p` is v[0], `*(p + 2)` is v[2] and `p[3]` is v[3].

questions.prompt: What happens when you read `v[5]` in `int v[5]`?
questions.explain: C never checks array bounds. Reading or writing outside the array is undefined behaviour: garbage, a crash, or silent corruption.
options: Undefined behaviour: the index is out of range and C does not check it
The program always stops with an error
option_notes: No automatic check exists in C.

questions.prompt: What is `sizeof(a)` for `int a[10]` on a system where an int has 4 bytes?
questions.explain: `sizeof` of an array is the size of the whole array: 10 elements * 4 bytes.
option_notes: That is the number of elements.
That is the size of one element.
That would be the size of a pointer.

questions.prompt: Which statements about arrays and pointers are true?
questions.explain: Indexing is defined through pointer arithmetic, and `sizeof` knows the full size of a real array. The array name is not an assignable variable, and a pointer carries no length.
options: An array name can be assigned a new address like a pointer
`sizeof(v)` of a real array gives its total size in bytes
A pointer parameter `int *v` knows how many elements the caller's array has
option_notes: False: pass the length as another parameter.

questions.prompt: In `int v[8];` the valid indices go from 0 to {{0}}.
questions.explain: An array of N elements has the indices 0 to N - 1.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a linear search in the array `v` for the value `x` in order.
questions.explain: A linear search looks at the elements one by one until it finds the value or runs out of elements.
items: If they are equal, stop: found at i
Otherwise move to the next index
If the end is reached, x is not present

questions.prompt: Match each array expression with its meaning for `int m[3][4]`.
questions.explain: A two-dimensional array is an array of rows, stored row after row in memory.
pairs: the size of one row: 4 * sizeof(int) bytes
the first row (an array of 4 ints)
